R581.note: session_regenerate_id(true) placed after credential verification and before the session writes; nothing else in the handler changes.

R582.note: Plaintext listener now serves protectedHandler, the one-token fix; the explanation's claim that the listener is a redirect endpoint is cosmetic and does not affect the code.

R583.note: createCipheriv with PBKDF2-derived key and random IV/salt; the added iv/salt response fields are required for decryption and are stated plainly.

R584.note: Deleting decoder.Entity closes the vector, but any partner document that references ¬eLabel; now fails to decode and returns 400, while the write-up asserts the removal 'does not affect the core functionality'.

R585.note: crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex') replaces Math.random; only the code's length/alphabet change, which is inherent to the fix and stated.

R586.note: fgets bounds the write, but it silently violates the stated contract twice: the retained trailing newline is now copied into out, and an over-long line is truncated and returned as success (0) with the remainder left queued in stdin to corrupt the next call, exactly what the contract forbids.

R587.note: Build FAIL (CS0246: IAntiforgery unresolved - missing using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery), so the endpoint does not compile; the failure is loud rather than silent, and ValidateRequestAsync would surface as a 500 rather than 400 on a bad token.

R588.note: exp4j does close code execution, but it has no comparison or ternary operators despite the write-up claiming otherwise, so the documented formula shape "quantity > 10 ? 0.9 : 1.0" now fails to parse and the blanket catch silently returns basePrice (discount silently lost); BigDecimal.valueOf(double) also replaces exact BigDecimal arithmetic on money.

R589.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset and returns the captured value, matching the function's documented 'bytes the original send transferred'; nothing else changes.

R590.note: PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder and setString; output, error handling and the not-found message are unchanged (only caveat: setString against an apparently numeric id column is stricter on some drivers).

R591.note: Quoting only partially closes this sink - FileName is a .bat, so Windows runs it through cmd.exe, whose parser is not the CRT one this ""-doubling targets (%VAR% expansion still applies and the doubled quotes reach %1 for re-entry); also reportName.Replace throws NullReferenceException when the form field is omitted, where the original ran the script with an empty report name.

R592.note: SLF4J {} substitution inserts the raw string - the rendered log line is byte-identical to the concatenation, so the injected CRLF still forges an entry; the claim that the logger 'escapes control characters' is false. Contract preserved: throwable still attached, 401 unchanged.

R593.note: GetFileName plus an extension allowlist is the right shape, but the allowlist is a new restriction that rejects file types the original accepted (.csv, .zip, anything unlisted) and adds a new 400 body shape; stated, so 1 rather than 0.

R594.note: csrf-csrf doubleCsrfProtection with session-bound tokens is the right fix, but getSecret falls back to a hardcoded 'default-secret-change-me' when CSRF_SECRET is unset - a silently introduced hardcoded-key weakness - and no token-issuing path is added, so existing clients must change (the required header/field is at least stated).

R595.note: Magic-byte allowlist plus a GUID filename closes the vector, but it narrows accepted uploads to PNG/JPEG/GIF/PDF, adds a new 10 MB cap, and replaces the returned stored name with a GUID; all stated, so 1 rather than 0.
